title: What, Where, Who: WH-Questions with be
objective: Ask for personal information with what, where and who, using falling intonation.
intro_md: [L1: In this lesson you ask for personal information with what, where and who. You already know two of these questions! In WH-questions your voice goes DOWN at the end: Where are you from?]
notes: TODO_audio: ex3 (Where is she from?, 0.75x), ex6 (Where are you from? falling contour, 1.0x), ex8 speaking model prompt. Band map §15 allots L10 no new vocabulary (grammar G7 only): what/where/who are function words and both anchor chunks were taught in L03/L05.

exercises.prompt: what · where · who · What's your name? · Where are you from?
exercises.rationale: Reactivates the two question chunks learners already own and isolates the three WH-words inside them — the lesson generalizes from chunk to system.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Match each question to its answer.]
exercises.rationale: Each WH-word maps to an information type — thing, place, person; the selection decision, not the syntax, is the new content of this lesson.

exercises.prompt: [audio, 0.75x] 'Where is she from?' — [L1: What does the speaker want to know?]
exercises.rationale: Comprehension check on the WH-word alone: learners often key on the sentence frame and answer the wrong question in real conversation.

options.label: A country.
options.rationale: where asks about a place — here, the country she is from.

options.label: A name.
options.rationale: Transfers from the more familiar What's-your-name chunk; catches frame-matching instead of WH-word listening.

options.label: A language.
options.rationale: Plausible topic from L06 conversations; forces attention to where, not to the general topic of introductions.

exercises.prompt: A: ___ is your teacher?  B: My teacher is Ana.  A: ___ is she from?  B: She's from Brazil.
exercises.rationale: Forced choice among WH-words over identical be-syntax; What in the bank catches the highest-frequency confusion (what/who for people), Is catches yes/no-question carryover from L09.
Unpacks the fossilized What's into what + is, showing the same inversion learners drilled in L09 — the chunk becomes analyzable grammar.

exercises.prompt: [audio, 1.0x] 'Where are you from?' — [L1: At the end, does the voice go up or down?]
exercises.rationale: P3 contrast with L09: WH-questions fall while yes/no questions rise; melody is the only audible difference between friendly and confused-sounding questions.

options.label: Down.
options.rationale: WH-questions end with falling intonation — the WH-word already signals the question.

options.label: Up.
options.rationale: Transfer from the L09 yes/no melody (and from zh/vi question rises); rising WH-questions sound like disbelief in English.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Ask it in English: '¿Quién es tu profesora?']
exercises.rationale: Maps es quién onto who while keeping be-inversion; blocks the frequent 'Who is she your teacher?' double-subject blend by requiring the clean frame.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Ask the AI about its country: ask with where, and let your voice fall at the end.]
asr_focus: are present between where and you (no 'Where you from?')
exercises.rationale: Produces the falling contour on a known chunk; ASR checks the copula that zh/vi/ar speakers drop inside WH-questions.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Interview the AI: ask its name, its country, and who its teacher is. Then the AI asks you the same three questions — answer them.]
exercises.rationale: G7's communicative need is getting personal information; the symmetric interview forces both question production and answer production with all three WH-words.
